intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn to say how much of a quality something has, and what that means: It was so hot that we stayed inside. This coffee is too sweet for me. She's old enough to vote. Warm-up: is the weather in your city too hot, or is it cool enough for you?
teachingNotes: so + adjective or adverb (no noun after it): so hot, so tired, so fast, so well. such + (a/an) + (adjective) + noun: such a good film (singular countable → such a/an), such nice people (plural → no a), such good weather (uncountable → no a). The quick test is the LAST word of the phrase: an adjective/adverb → so; a noun (kata benda) → such. Common error: *'It was so a good film' → It was such a good film. Also *'such good film' (missing a with a singular noun) and *'They are so nice people'. Explain 'adjective' (kata sifat), 'adverb' (kata keterangan cara, known from a2-adverbs-manner) and 'noun' (kata benda) in plain words the first time.

Result: so … that / such … that + what happened (It was so hot that we stayed inside; It was such a good film that I watched it twice). Indonesian 'begitu … sehingga …'. In speaking, 'that' is often dropped (I was so tired I fell asleep): accept it. Without 'that', so/such add feeling like 'banget' (It's so hot! She's such a kind person!). Don't confuse with the linker so = jadi from a2-linkers-sequence (I was tired, so I went home). so many / so much + noun (so many people, so much traffic) looks like a broken rule: many/much are quantity words, not describing words, so so goes before them; mention it, don't test it. 'such a lot of' exists: only if asked.

too + adjective/adverb = more than is OK, a PROBLEM (terlalu): too small, too expensive, too fast. Add to + verb for what you can't do (too tired to drive, too young to vote) or for + person (too expensive for me). Common error: *'This bag is too much expensive' → too expensive: too much goes before uncountable nouns (too much sugar, from a2-countable-uncountable) or after a verb (You work too much), never before an adjective. Indonesian trap: casual Indonesian uses 'terlalu' as praise (terlalu enak, terlalu cantik); in English too is never praise: *'This food is too delicious' sounds like a complaint. For praise use so / really / very. very only describes (very hot, but we can go out); too says there's a problem (too hot to go out). Also: 'too' at the end of a sentence = juga (I like it too); to / too / two sound the same.

enough = cukup, as much as needed. It goes AFTER an adjective or adverb (old enough, big enough, fast enough) but BEFORE a noun (enough money, enough chairs, enough time). Say it like this so it doesn't look like a broken rule: after describing words, before thing words. Common error: *'He is enough old to drive' → old enough (Indonesian 'cukup tua/cukup umur' puts cukup first). Negative: not … enough (The room isn't big enough; He doesn't speak loudly enough). + to + verb (old enough to drive) or for + person/thing (big enough for six people). too and not … enough often mean the same problem: too small = not big enough; too young = not old enough. Pronunciation: enough = 'i-NAF'.

The 'cukup' trap: Indonesian 'cukup' means both enough (as much as needed) and quite (= lumayan, taught in a2-adverbs-manner). 'Kamarnya cukup besar' can be The room is quite big (lumayan besar, just a description) or The room is big enough (for what we need). If there's a need or purpose (untuk …, for us, to …), use enough; if it's just a description, use quite.

Limits: A0–A2 grammar only (present and past simple, past continuous, can/could, will, going to, should/have to, comparatives). Don't teach so + adjective + a + noun (so good a film, literary), too + adjective + a + noun (too big a risk), 'so as to', 'such that', 'enough of', or enough as a pronoun (That's enough!) unless asked. No second conditional (*'If it were cheaper …'), no relative clauses beyond fixed phrases, no passive.

keyPoints.title: so, such and the result with that
keyPoints.explanation: so goes before an adjective or adverb with no noun after it: so hot, so fast. such goes before a phrase that ends with a noun: such a good film (one thing → such a/an), such nice people, such good weather (plural or uncountable → no a). Not 'so a good film'. Add that + what happened to show the result: It was so hot that we stayed inside.

keyPoints.title: too + adjective (+ to + verb) = a problem
keyPoints.explanation: too means more than is OK, so there's a problem (terlalu): This shirt is too small. Add to + verb for what you can't do: He's too young to vote. Before an adjective it's just too, not 'too much expensive' (too much goes before uncountable nouns: too much sugar). too is never praise: for 'enak banget' say so delicious or really delicious, not 'too delicious'.

keyPoints.title: (not) adjective + enough
keyPoints.explanation: enough means as much as you need (cukup). It goes after an adjective or adverb: old enough, big enough. Negative: not … enough: The room isn't big enough. Add to + verb or for + someone: She's old enough to vote. Before a noun, enough comes first: enough money, enough time. So: after describing words, before thing words. Not 'enough old'.

material.title: so or such? Look at the last word

blocks.text:
Both **so** and **such** make something stronger, with feeling, a bit like *banget* or *sekali*. Which one you use depends on the words that come after it.
- **so** + an **adjective** (a describing word: *hot, tired, kind*) or an **adverb** (a word that says how: *fast, well, slowly*), with **no noun** after it: *It's **so** hot today! She drives **so** fast.*
- **such** + a phrase that **ends with a noun** (a thing or person word: *film, people, weather*): *It was **such** a good film!*

With such, check the noun: one countable thing → **such a/an** (*such a good film, such an old car*); plural or uncountable → **such** without a (*such nice people, such good weather*). So the quick test is the **last word**: a describing word → **so**; a noun → **such**.

id.text:
**so** dan **such** sama-sama membuat sesuatu lebih kuat, dengan perasaan, mirip *banget* atau *sekali*. Mana yang dipakai tergantung kata-kata setelahnya.
- **so** + **kata sifat** (adjective, kata yang menjelaskan: *hot, tired, kind*) atau **adverb** (kata yang menjelaskan cara: *fast, well, slowly*), **tanpa kata benda** setelahnya: *It's **so** hot today!* (Panas banget hari ini!) *She drives **so** fast.*
- **such** + frasa yang **berakhir dengan kata benda** (noun, kata untuk benda atau orang: *film, people, weather*): *It was **such** a good film!* (Filmnya bagus banget!)

Kalau pakai such, cek kata bendanya: satu benda yang bisa dihitung → **such a/an** (*such a good film, such an old car*); jamak atau tak terhitung → **such** tanpa a (*such nice people, such good weather*). Jadi tes cepatnya adalah **kata terakhir**: kata sifat → **so**; kata benda → **such**.

id.note: so + kata sifat (tanpa kata benda setelahnya)

rows.en: It was such a good film!

id.note: such a + kata sifat + satu benda

rows.en: My colleagues are such nice people.
rows.id: Rekan-rekan kerja saya orangnya baik-baik sekali.

id.note: such + kata benda tak terhitung (tanpa a)

blocks.text: **Looks like a broken rule: so many, so much.** You'll hear *There were **so many** people at the station* and *There's **so much** traffic*. Here so comes before a noun phrase, but that's because **many** and **much** are quantity words (*banyak*), not describing words: so + many / much is fine. With a describing word before a noun, it's still such: *such **long** queues*.

id.text: **Kelihatannya melanggar aturan: so many, so much.** Kamu akan mendengar *There were **so many** people at the station* (banyak sekali orang di stasiun) dan *There's **so much** traffic* (macet banget). Di sini so ada sebelum kata benda, tapi itu karena **many** dan **much** adalah kata jumlah (*banyak*), bukan kata sifat: so + many / much boleh. Kalau ada kata sifat sebelum kata bendanya, tetap pakai such: *such **long** queues* (antrean yang panjang sekali).

id.title: so atau such? Lihat kata terakhirnya

material.title: The result: so … that, such … that

blocks.text:
To say what happened **because** something was very strong, add **that** + the result (*akibatnya*). Indonesian says *begitu … sehingga …*:
- **so** + adjective/adverb + **that** …: *It was **so** hot **that** we stayed inside.*
- **such** + (a/an) + adjective + noun + **that** …: *It was **such** a good film **that** I watched it twice.*

In conversation people often drop **that**: *I was so tired I fell asleep on the KRL.* Both are correct.

id.text:
Untuk mengatakan apa yang terjadi **karena** sesuatu sangat kuat, tambahkan **that** + akibatnya. Bahasa Indonesia bilang *begitu … sehingga …*:
- **so** + kata sifat/adverb + **that** …: *It was **so** hot **that** we stayed inside.* (Cuacanya begitu panas sehingga kami tetap di dalam.)
- **such** + (a/an) + kata sifat + kata benda + **that** …: *It was **such** a good film **that** I watched it twice.* (Filmnya begitu bagus sehingga saya menontonnya dua kali.)

Dalam percakapan, orang sering tidak memakai **that**: *I was so tired I fell asleep on the KRL.* Keduanya benar.

rows.id: Jalannya begitu banjir sehingga busnya putar balik.

rows.en: Sari spoke so quietly that nobody heard her.
rows.id: Sari bicara begitu pelan sehingga tidak ada yang mendengarnya.

id.note: such a + kata sifat + kata benda + that

rows.en: They were such friendly neighbours that we still visit them.
rows.id: Mereka tetangga yang begitu ramah sehingga kami masih mengunjungi mereka.

blocks.text: **Two different so's.** You know **so** = *jadi* from linkers: *I was tired, **so** I went home* (comma, then the result). In this lesson **so** goes **before a describing word**: *I was **so** tired **that** I went home.* Same idea, different grammar. And don't mix **that** with *than* (from comparatives): not 'so hot than'.

id.text: **Dua so yang berbeda.** Kamu sudah kenal **so** = *jadi* dari pelajaran kata penghubung: *I was tired, **so** I went home* (koma, lalu akibatnya). Di pelajaran ini **so** ada **sebelum kata sifat**: *I was **so** tired **that** I went home.* Idenya sama, tata bahasanya beda. Dan jangan tertukar **that** dengan *than* (dari perbandingan): bukan 'so hot than'.

options: The test was so easy that everyone passed.
The test was such easy that everyone passed.
The test was so easy than everyone passed.
blocks.explain: easy is a describing word with no noun after it, so it's so … that. such needs a noun (such an easy test), and the result word is that, not than.

id.explain: easy adalah kata sifat tanpa kata benda setelahnya, jadi pakai so … that. such butuh kata benda (such an easy test), dan kata untuk akibat adalah that, bukan than.

blocks.text:
**too** = *terlalu*: more than is OK, so there's a **problem**. Compare:
- *It's **very** hot, but we can go out.* (just a description)
- *It's **too** hot to go out.* (a problem: we can't)

Add **to + verb** for what you can't do: *He's **too** young **to** vote.* Or **for** + a person: *The rent is **too** expensive **for** us.* Before an adjective it's just **too**, never 'too much expensive': **too much** goes before **uncountable nouns** (*too much sugar*) or after a verb (*You work too much*), and **too many** before plural nouns (*too many cars*).

id.text:
**too** = *terlalu*: lebih dari yang wajar, jadi ada **masalah**. Bandingkan:
- *It's **very** hot, but we can go out.* (sangat panas, tapi kita bisa keluar: hanya menjelaskan)
- *It's **too** hot to go out.* (terlalu panas untuk keluar: masalah, kita tidak bisa)

Tambahkan **to + kata kerja** untuk hal yang tidak bisa dilakukan: *He's **too** young **to** vote.* (Dia terlalu muda untuk ikut pemilu.) Atau **for** + orang: *The rent is **too** expensive **for** us.* (Sewanya terlalu mahal untuk kami.) Sebelum kata sifat cukup **too** saja, jangan pernah 'too much expensive': **too much** dipakai sebelum **kata benda tak terhitung** (*too much sugar*) atau setelah kata kerja (*You work too much*), dan **too many** sebelum kata benda jamak (*too many cars*).

rows.id: Kemeja ini terlalu kecil. Ada ukuran medium?

rows.en: My nephew is too young to vote.
rows.id: Keponakan saya terlalu muda untuk ikut pemilu.

id.note: too + kata sifat + to + kata kerja

rows.en: The ojek driver was going too fast.
This coffee has too much sugar.

id.note: too much + kata benda tak terhitung

blocks.text: **The terlalu trap.** In casual Indonesian, *terlalu* can be praise: *Masakannya terlalu enak!* In English **too** is **always a problem**. *This food is too delicious* sounds like a complaint (so delicious that it's bad?). For praise, say **so**, **really** or **very**: *This food is so delicious!* Also: **too** at the end of a sentence means *juga* (*I like it too*), and **to, too, two** all sound the same: 'tuu'.

id.text: **Jebakan terlalu.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia santai, *terlalu* bisa jadi pujian: *Masakannya terlalu enak!* Dalam bahasa Inggris **too** **selalu berarti masalah**. *This food is too delicious* terdengar seperti keluhan (enaknya kelewatan sampai jadi masalah?). Untuk memuji, pakai **so**, **really** atau **very**: *This food is so delicious!* Selain itu: **too** di akhir kalimat artinya *juga* (*I like it too*), dan **to, too, two** bunyinya sama: 'tuu'.

options: This coffee is too much sweet.
blocks.explain: Before an adjective (sweet) it's just too: too sweet. too much goes before uncountable nouns (too much sugar). 'enough sweet' has enough in the wrong place, and it would mean something else.

id.explain: Sebelum kata sifat (sweet) cukup too saja: too sweet. too much dipakai sebelum kata benda tak terhitung (too much sugar). 'enough sweet' salah letak enough-nya, dan artinya juga lain.

material.title: enough: after describing words, before nouns

blocks.text:
**enough** (say 'i-NAF') = *cukup*: as much as you need. Its place depends on the word it goes with:
- **after** an adjective or adverb: *old **enough**, big **enough**, loudly **enough***.
- **before** a noun: ***enough** money, **enough** chairs, **enough** time*.

This isn't a broken rule, it's two patterns: after describing words, before thing words. The Indonesian trap is *cukup besar*, with cukup first, which makes people say 'enough big'. In English it's **big enough**.

Negative: **not … enough**: *The table **isn't** big **enough**.* Add **to + verb** or **for** + someone: *She's old enough **to** vote. The table isn't big enough **for** eight people.* Often **too** and **not … enough** say the same problem: *too young = not old enough*.

id.text:
**enough** (dibaca 'i-NAF') = *cukup*: sebanyak yang dibutuhkan. Letaknya tergantung kata yang menyertainya:
- **setelah** kata sifat atau adverb: *old **enough** (cukup umur), big **enough** (cukup besar), loudly **enough** (cukup keras)*.
- **sebelum** kata benda: ***enough** money (cukup uang), **enough** chairs, **enough** time*.

Ini bukan aturan yang dilanggar, tapi dua pola: setelah kata sifat, sebelum kata benda. Jebakan bahasa Indonesia ada di *cukup besar*, dengan cukup di depan, sehingga orang bilang 'enough big'. Dalam bahasa Inggris: **big enough**.

Bentuk negatif: **not … enough**: *The table **isn't** big **enough**.* (Mejanya kurang besar.) Tambahkan **to + kata kerja** atau **for** + seseorang: *She's old enough **to** vote. The table isn't big enough **for** eight people.* Sering kali **too** dan **not … enough** menyatakan masalah yang sama: *too young = not old enough* (terlalu muda = belum cukup umur).

rows.en: My sister is old enough to vote now.
rows.id: Kakak perempuan saya sekarang sudah cukup umur untuk ikut pemilu.

rows.en: This table isn't big enough for eight people.
rows.id: Meja ini tidak cukup besar untuk delapan orang.

rows.en: He doesn't speak loudly enough in meetings.
rows.id: Dia bicaranya kurang keras di rapat.

rows.en: Do we have enough chairs for the meeting?
rows.id: Apakah kursi kita cukup untuk rapat?

blocks.text: **cukup = enough or quite?** Indonesian *cukup* has two meanings. *Kamarnya cukup besar* can be **The room is quite big** (lumayan besar: just a description, from the adverbs lesson) or **The room is big enough** (for what we need). Trick: if there's a need or a purpose (*untuk …*, for us, to + verb), use **enough**. If you're only describing, use **quite**.

id.text: **cukup = enough atau quite?** Kata *cukup* punya dua arti. *Kamarnya cukup besar* bisa berarti **The room is quite big** (lumayan besar: hanya menjelaskan, dari pelajaran adverb) atau **The room is big enough** (sesuai yang kita butuhkan). Triknya: kalau ada kebutuhan atau tujuan (*untuk …*, for us, to + kata kerja), pakai **enough**. Kalau hanya menjelaskan, pakai **quite**.

options: We don't have enough of chairs.
blocks.explain: chairs is a noun, and enough goes before a noun: enough chairs. After a describing word it's the other way round (big enough).

id.explain: chairs adalah kata benda, dan enough ada sebelum kata benda: enough chairs. Setelah kata sifat urutannya terbalik (big enough).

id.title: enough: setelah kata sifat, sebelum kata benda

suggestedQuestions: How do I know when to use so and when to use such?
What's the difference between very and too?
Why is it 'old enough' but 'enough money'?

flashcards.back: It was such a good film! (not 'so a good film')

resources.title: Intensifiers: 'so' and 'such'
resources.note: A B1–B2 grammar page on so + adjective/adverb, such + (a/an) + adjective + noun and so/such … that for results, with two short tests. It also covers so much / so many and so much + comparatives, which go a little beyond this lesson.

id.note: Halaman tata bahasa B1–B2 tentang so + kata sifat/adverb, such + (a/an) + kata sifat + kata benda, dan so/such … that untuk akibat, dengan dua tes singkat. Halaman ini juga membahas so much / so many dan so much + perbandingan, yang sedikit di luar pelajaran ini.

resources.title: Using 'enough'
resources.note: A B1–B2 grammar page on where enough goes: after adjectives and adverbs, before nouns, with two multiple-choice tests. It also shows verb + enough and enough of, which this lesson doesn't teach, and it doesn't cover too.

id.note: Halaman tata bahasa B1–B2 tentang letak enough: setelah kata sifat dan adverb, sebelum kata benda, dengan dua tes pilihan ganda. Halaman ini juga menunjukkan kata kerja + enough dan enough of, yang tidak diajarkan di pelajaran ini, dan tidak membahas too.

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar mengatakan seberapa kuat sebuah sifat, dan apa akibatnya: It was so hot that we stayed inside (cuacanya begitu panas sehingga kami tetap di dalam). This coffee is too sweet for me (kopi ini terlalu manis untuk saya). She's old enough to vote (dia sudah cukup umur untuk ikut pemilu). Pemanasan: apakah cuaca di kotamu too hot (terlalu panas), atau cukup sejuk untukmu?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana aku tahu kapan pakai so dan kapan pakai such?

assessment.sst-1: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Bu Ani is ___ a kind teacher that all her students love her.
assessment.sst-2: Gabungkan kedua kalimat dengan so … that: The KRL was very crowded. We couldn't get on.
assessment.sst-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya dengan mengganti satu kata: We had so a good time in Bali.
assessment.sst-4: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: This suitcase is ___ heavy to take on the plane, so Budi has to check it in.
assessment.sst-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: This laptop is too much expensive for me.
assessment.sst-6: Sebuah situs menolak kata sandi barumu. Perbaiki kesalahan di pesannya: Your password isn't enough strong.
assessment.sst-7: Tulis ulang dengan not … enough dan lawan kata dari small: The hall is too small for 200 guests.
